title: With/Without
program_note:
With/Without is one part of a large number of pieces intended for dance, inspired by the play “Desire Under the Elms” by Eugene O’Neill.  This piece is designed to be performable with any combination of the three instruments:  thus, three different solos, three different duos, and the trio are all intended to be equally legitimate.

Each individual line has its own character, which should be explored and exploited choreographically.  The idea is that interspersed in an evening of dance, in the progression from solos through duos to trios, the recurrence of each instruments’ lines would become familiar to the audience but—since the lines would be recontextualized—would not seem repetitive.

The title and subtitle refer to the way that each part can function both with (“con-”) and without (“sol-”) the other parts, and to the consoling affect of the flute line.

With/Without is approximately seven minutes in duration, although the harp solo and flute solo versions are somewhat shorter.

David S. Lefkowitz

1 May 2003

Los Angeles, California
